editorial.headline: Government Film Distribution: No PMA Route in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This government-managed distribution activity spans films, video, television programmes and audiovisual rights, but it is closed to foreign ownership nationally and cannot be registered as PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
**This activity concerns the government-managed distribution of screen work, rather than its production.** It covers distributing films, videos, television programmes and comparable audiovisual works to cinemas and feature-film theatres, television networks and stations, and exhibition organisers, where the activity is managed by government for remuneration. The remit also reaches government-managed distribution of film, video and television programming carrying sports-media content. Just as importantly, it includes the government-managed acquisition of distribution rights in films, videos, audiovisual works and similar products. The category therefore follows both the movement of content to its outlets and the securing of the rights that make that movement possible.

The defined operator matters. This is a government-managed activity, not a broad label for any commercial handling of a screen title. Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the scale field is deliberately broad; it does not alter the category’s government-managed character. A careful reading keeps the work anchored to its stated destinations—cinemas, television networks and stations, and exhibition organisers—and to the stated commercial footing of remuneration. The scope names those destinations directly rather than leaving them implicit. Sports-media content appears within the category only where its distribution is government-managed, while distribution-rights acquisition belongs to that same governmental remit.

The ownership position is unambiguous at national level. The PMA status is TERTUTUP, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 0%. In practical terms, a foreign investor cannot hold an ownership stake under this activity nationally. That conclusion does not depend on the scale at which the activity is registered: the record’s scale availability and its foreign-ownership position answer different questions. One states which scales are open; the other fixes the foreign-ownership boundary. The record identifies Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source for that national PMA position.

Bali is equally clear, and no more permissive. The activity is marked TERTUTUP and blocked for PMA registration there because the national position is closed to foreign ownership. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali record also identifies an island-wide, permanent provincial moratorium rule for PMA, cited to a Gubernur letter. It does not create a Bali-only ownership allowance or a different route around the national closure. For founders assessing this single activity, the conclusion is precise: its governmental distribution scope is specific, its available scales are stated, and its foreign-ownership line is closed both nationally and in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner cannot register this government-managed distribution activity as PMA in Bali today.
